title: Which Way
logline: On the back roads of the dry zone, with no signs and no signal, Chathura keeps stopping to ask the way. Every person points somewhere different, and every answer comes with a small piece of a life.
human_question: When everyone points a different way, how do you decide which road to take?

premise.story: A real journey across unsigned rural roads to a destination Chathura genuinely does not know how to reach. The film is made of the people he asks: a shopkeeper, a farmer on a tractor, children on bicycles, a bus conductor. Each gives directions from where they stand.
premise.place: Dry-zone back roads: red earth, tank bunds, junctions with a single boutique, scrub jungle, the heat of midday.
premise.experience: The low, looping feeling of being lost, carried by the warmth and variety of strangers who stop to help.

concept_links.why: The plain inability to settle on what is in front of you, and the flat, stalled feeling that comes with it [C008-P:L30; C008-P:L34]. The film shows an unsettled decision, not anyone's spiritual doubt.

Among the helps the source lists against doubt is simply asking a lot of questions; it also says ordinary uncertainty about something not yet known may not be a fault at all. The film honours the asking.

what_camera_could_observe: Junctions with no signs; the car or motorbike slowing, stopping, turning back
Hands pointing in different directions; directions given by landmarks ('past the big tamarind tree')
The short conversations that open up while directions are given
The moment a road is finally chosen, and where it actually leads
what_must_be_real: The journey and being lost must be genuine. The people asked are met by chance and appear only with their consent. No one is made to look foolish.

possible_arc.opening: A junction, three roads, dust, and no idea.
possible_arc.turn: The answers start to contradict each other, and the strangers become more interesting than the destination.
possible_arc.ending_open: Chathura arrives somewhere, or does not. Wherever the road really ends is the ending.

position_hint: opening candidate: the most literal first film for a group called Lost; an Object 4 acquisition could happen only if a stranger on the road genuinely gives or trades something

requirements: A real destination reached by poorly signed rural roads
Low mobile coverage along the route
Freedom to stop and film brief encounters with consent

suggestions.name: Back roads of Monaragala district
suggestions.why: A large, thinly populated dry-zone district with many minor roads between villages and tanks.
suggestions.season_notes: Dry season for dust and heat; inter-monsoon rains change road conditions
suggestions.verify: Choose a real destination first; confirm route conditions and coverage.

risks: Sliding into a staged metaphor or a travel vlog
Chathura becoming the subject rather than the people he meets
Consent from people filmed in passing
drop_if: The route turns out to be easy to follow
It can only work if set up, rather than genuinely lived

connections.note: The other opening candidate: a place lost rather than a traveller lost.
Both watch a decision that will not settle, one on land and one at the water's edge.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
